question.:question/problem:
Given that
$$
\displaystyle D=\begin{bmatrix}5 & -5 & 5 \\ -8 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & x\end{bmatrix}
$$ 
and $det(D)=-42,$ find the value of $x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(5)\begin{vmatrix}0 & 5 \\ 1 & x\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(5)((0)(x)-(5)(1)) \\  & =(5)(-5) \\  & =-25\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(-5)\begin{vmatrix}-8 & 5 \\ 3 & x\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(-5)((-8)(x)-(5)(3)) \\  & =-(-5)(- 8 x - 15) \\  & =- 40 x - 75\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(5)\begin{vmatrix}-8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(5)((-8)(1)-(0)(3)) \\  & =(5)(-8) \\  & =-40\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =- 40 x - 140\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}- 40 x - 140 & =-42 \\ - 40 x & =98 \\ x & =- \frac{49}{20}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=- \frac{49}{20}$.

question.:question/problem: Given that $B=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -3 & 5 \\ m & 1 & m \\ -1 & 4 & -2\end{bmatrix}$ and $det(B)=52,$ find the value of $m.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(-5)\begin{vmatrix}1 & m \\ 4 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(-5)((1)(-2)-(m)(4)) \\  & =(-5)(- 4 m - 2) \\  & =20 m + 10\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(-3)\begin{vmatrix}m & m \\ -1 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(-3)((m)(-2)-(m)(-1)) \\  & =-(-3)(- m) \\  & =- 3 m\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(5)\begin{vmatrix}m & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(5)((m)(4)-(1)(-1)) \\  & =(5)(4 m + 1) \\  & =20 m + 5\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =37 m + 15\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}37 m + 15 & =52 \\ 37 m & =37 \\ m & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $m=1$.

question.:question/problem: Find the possible values of the constant $p$ given that the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & -5 & 2 \\ 6 & -5 & 2 p - 4\end{bmatrix}$ is singular.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(1)\begin{vmatrix}-5 & 2 \\ -5 & 2 p - 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)((-5)(2 p - 4)-(2)(-5)) \\  & =(1)(30 - 10 p) \\  & =30 - 10 p\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(0)\begin{vmatrix}5 & 2 \\ 6 & 2 p - 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(0)((5)(2 p - 4)-(2)(6)) \\  & =-(0)(10 p - 32) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(1)\begin{vmatrix}5 & -5 \\ 6 & -5\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)((5)(-5)-(-5)(6)) \\  & =(1)(5) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =35 - 10 p\end{aligned}
$$

A singular matrix has determinant $0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}35 - 10 p & =0 \\ - 10 p & =-35 \\ p & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $p=\frac{7}{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Given that the determinant of $\begin{bmatrix}x & 2 x & -5 \\ 3 & x & 5 \\ 7 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$ is $369$, find all the possible values of $x$ **in ascending order**.

In ascending order, $x=$
{{field-1}} and $x=$
{{field-2}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(x)\begin{vmatrix}x & 5 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(x)((x)(2)-(5)(1)) \\  & =(x)(2 x - 5) \\  & =2 x^{2} - 5 x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(2 x)\begin{vmatrix}3 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(2 x)((3)(2)-(5)(7)) \\  & =-(2 x)(-29) \\  & =58 x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(-5)\begin{vmatrix}3 & x \\ 7 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(-5)((3)(1)-(x)(7)) \\  & =(-5)(3 - 7 x) \\  & =35 x - 15\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =2 x^{2} + 88 x - 15\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} + 88 x - 15 & =369 \\ 2 x^{2} + 88 x - 384 & =0 \\ x & =\frac{-(88)\pm\sqrt{(88)^2-4(2)(-384)}}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{-88\pm 104}{4} \\ x & =-48,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in **ascending order**, the solutions are $x=-48$ and $x=4$.

question.:question/problem:
Given that the determinant of
$$
\displaystyle \begin{bmatrix}x & 2 x & 3 \\ 5 & x & 7 \\ 3 & 5 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$
is $40$, find all the possible values of $x.$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(x)\begin{vmatrix}x & 7 \\ 5 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(x)((x)(1)-(7)(5)) \\  & =(x)(x - 35) \\  & =x^{2} - 35 x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(2 x)\begin{vmatrix}5 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(2 x)((5)(1)-(7)(3)) \\  & =-(2 x)(-16) \\  & =32 x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(3)\begin{vmatrix}5 & x \\ 3 & 5\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(3)((5)(5)-(x)(3)) \\  & =(3)(25 - 3 x) \\  & =75 - 9 x\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =x^{2} - 12 x + 75\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}x^{2} - 12 x + 75 & =40 \\ x^{2} - 12 x + 35 & =0 \\ x & =\frac{-(-12)\pm\sqrt{(-12)^2-4(1)(35)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{12\pm 2}{2} \\ x & =5,\,7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=5$ and $x=7$.

question.:question/problem:
Given that $M=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -5 & 2 \\ 5 & p & 0 \\ p - 3 & 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}$ and $det(M)=-33,$ find all the possible values of $p.$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(0)\begin{vmatrix}p & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(0)((p)(-1)-(0)(0)) \\  & =(0)(- p) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(-5)\begin{vmatrix}5 & 0 \\ p - 3 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(-5)((5)(-1)-(0)(p - 3)) \\  & =-(-5)(-5) \\  & =-25\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(2)\begin{vmatrix}5 & p \\ p - 3 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2)((5)(0)-(p)(p - 3)) \\  & =(2)(- p^{2} + 3 p) \\  & =- 2 p^{2} + 6 p\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =- 2 p^{2} + 6 p - 25\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}- 2 p^{2} + 6 p - 25 & =-33 \\ - 2 p^{2} + 6 p + 8 & =0 \\ p & =\frac{-(6)\pm\sqrt{(6)^2-4(-2)(8)}}{2(-2)} \\  & =\frac{-6\pm 10}{-4} \\ p & =-1,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $p=-1$ and $p=4$.

question.:question/problem:
Find, in **ascending order**, the values ​​of $x$ for which the following matrix is singular.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}x - 5 & 2 x & 4 \\ 5 & x & x + 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$

In ascending order, $x=$
{{field-1}} and $x=$
{{field-2}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(x - 5)\begin{vmatrix}x & x + 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(x - 5)((x)(3)-(x + 1)(0)) \\  & =(x - 5)(3 x) \\  & =3 x^{2} - 15 x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(2 x)\begin{vmatrix}5 & x + 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(2 x)((5)(3)-(x + 1)(1)) \\  & =-(2 x)(14 - x) \\  & =2 x^{2} - 28 x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(4)\begin{vmatrix}5 & x \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(4)((5)(0)-(x)(1)) \\  & =(4)(- x) \\  & =- 4 x\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =5 x^{2} - 47 x\end{aligned}
$$

A singular matrix has determinant $0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}5 x^{2} - 47 x & =0 \\ x (5 x - 47) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,\frac{47}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in **ascending order**, the solutions are $x=0$ and $x=\frac{47}{5}$.

question.:question/problem:
Find the possible values of the constant $k$ given that the matrix
$\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -1 & k \\ 5 & k & - k \\ 5 & k & k\end{bmatrix}$ is singular.

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(-5)\begin{vmatrix}k & - k \\ k & k\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(-5)((k)(k)-(- k)(k)) \\  & =(-5)(2 k^{2}) \\  & =- 10 k^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(-1)\begin{vmatrix}5 & - k \\ 5 & k\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(-1)((5)(k)-(- k)(5)) \\  & =-(-1)(10 k) \\  & =10 k\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(k)\begin{vmatrix}5 & k \\ 5 & k\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(k)((5)(k)-(k)(5)) \\  & =(k)(0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =- 10 k^{2} + 10 k\end{aligned}
$$

A singular matrix has determinant $0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}- 10 k^{2} + 10 k & =0 \\ - 10 k (k - 1) & =0 \\ k & =0,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=0$ and $k=1$.

question.:question/problem:
Given that the determinant of $\begin{bmatrix}x^{2} - 5 & 3 & 0 \\ x & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ is $39$, find all the possible values of $x$ **in ascending order**.

In ascending order, $x=$
{{field-1}} and $x=$
{{field-2}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(x^{2} - 5)\begin{vmatrix}5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(x^{2} - 5)((5)(0)-(-1)(4)) \\  & =(x^{2} - 5)(4) \\  & =4 x^{2} - 20\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(3)\begin{vmatrix}x & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(3)((x)(0)-(-1)(1)) \\  & =-(3)(1) \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(0)\begin{vmatrix}x & 5 \\ 1 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(0)((x)(4)-(5)(1)) \\  & =(0)(4 x - 5) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =4 x^{2} - 23\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}4 x^{2} - 23 & =39 \\ 4 x^{2} & =62 \\ x^2 & =\frac{31}{2} \\ x & =\pm\sqrt{\frac{31}{2}} \\ x & =- \frac{\sqrt{62}}{2},\,\frac{\sqrt{62}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in **ascending order**, the solutions are $x=- \frac{\sqrt{62}}{2}$ and $x=\frac{\sqrt{62}}{2}$.
